subject: general
question: While multitasking, which of the following best describes what happens when Alt + Tab is used repeatedly?

options.text: It cycles through open applications in the order of last use.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It cycles through open applications in the order of last use.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alt + Tab is a keyboard shortcut used in Microsoft Windows operating systems to **quickly switch between open applications.**
 
• When pressed repeatedly, Alt + Tab cycles through the currently open applications** in the order of their last use.**
 
• Holding down the Alt key while repeatedly pressing Tab allows the user to preview and select the desired application.
 
• This feature is especially useful for multitasking, enabling users to switch efficiently between different programs without using the mouse.
 
• The functionality is supported in most versions of Windows, including Windows 10 and Windows 11, and has been a staple feature since early Windows versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Task View:** Windows also offers a "Task View" feature that allows users to view all open applications and virtual desktops in a graphical interface. It can be accessed by pressing **Windows key + Tab.**
 
• **Alt + Esc:** Another related shortcut is Alt + Esc, which switches between open applications **without displaying the preview interface.**
 
• **Windows Snap Feature:** Windows provides a Snap feature for multitasking, allowing users to resize and position windows side by side. This can be accessed using **Windows key + Arrow keys.**
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts for Efficiency:** Common shortcuts like Ctrl + Tab (for cycling through tabs in browsers) and Windows key + D (to show the desktop) are designed to enhance productivity.
 
• **Application Switching in Other OS:** MacOS uses **Command + Tab** for application switching, similar to Alt + Tab in Windows, but with slight differences in behavior.
